type.description: What it is: common.client (Clients), common.http-endpoint (HTTP endpoint), common.service (Service), common.actor (Actors (keyed objects)), aws.region (Region), aws.vpc (VPC), aws.nat-gateway (NAT gateway), aws.vpc-endpoint (VPC endpoint), aws.apigateway (API Gateway), aws.cloudfront (CloudFront distribution), aws.lambda (Lambda function), aws.sqs (SQS queue), aws.sns (SNS topic), aws.dynamodb (DynamoDB table), aws.s3 (S3 bucket), aws.ses (SES email).

name.description: What the canvas calls it. Defaults to its id.

region.description: The provider's region it runs in. Absent means the provider's default, or the region box it is in.

parent.description: The id of the container (a region or VPC box) it sits inside.

position.description: Where it sits on the canvas. Absent means it is laid out automatically.

size.description: A container's box size, in canvas units.

settings.description: Only the settings you change; the rest take the component's defaults.

origin.description: Where it came from when imported, so a re-import can find and merge it.

edge.description: A connection: calls or messages from one node's output to another node.

port.description: The output it leaves from, when the node has several (deliver, dlq, onFailure...). Default out.

connector.description: What sits on it. Absent means the most specific one that fits: core.link (Link), core.poller (Poller), aws.sqs.event-source-mapping (Event source mapping).

settings.description: Only the settings you change: the port's, the connector's and transport's.

weight.title: Weight
weight.description: Share of traffic this edge gets when the source routes by weight.

operation.title: Operation
operation.description: What this call does to the receiver. Stores and object stores price and limit reads and writes differently. One of: read (Read), write (Write).

payload.title: Payload size
payload.description: Size of what this call carries. 0 keeps the size the sender gave it. In KB.

timeout.title: Timeout
timeout.description: How long the caller waits before giving up. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

cancelOnTimeout.title: Cancel on timeout
cancelOnTimeout.description: Off: the callee keeps working after the caller gives up (wasted work, like most real clients). On: the work is cancelled.

backoff.title: Initial backoff
backoff.description: A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

maxBackoff.title: Max backoff
maxBackoff.description: A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

jitter.title: Jitter
jitter.description: Randomise each wait between zero and its full length.

workers.title: Workers
workers.description: How many take a batch and call with it at the same time. Each waits for its call before taking more. In workers.

batchSize.title: Batch size
batchSize.description: Records taken for one call, at most. In records.

backoff.title: Pause after a failure
backoff.description: How long a worker waits after a failed call before it takes again. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

batchWindow.title: Batching window
batchWindow.description: How long to wait for a batch to fill. Standard queues only. The messages are already received, so their visibility timeout is running while the batch fills: AWS advises a visibility timeout of six times the function timeout plus this window. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes". A hard limit of the provider.

maxConcurrency.title: Maximum concurrency
maxConcurrency.description: Cap on concurrent invocations from this queue. 0 for none (the mapping then scales up to 1,250). AWS accepts 2 to 1,000, and not together with provisioned mode. In invocations. A hard limit of the provider.

initialConcurrency.title: Starting concurrency
initialConcurrency.description: A standard queue's mapping starts with 5 concurrent batches. AWS fixes this at 5; it is editable here to explore what-ifs. In invocations. A hard limit of the provider.

scaleUpPerMinute.title: Scale-up rate
scaleUpPerMinute.description: Invocations added each minute while messages are waiting, up to 1,250. AWS publishes this for standard queues only; the same ramp is used for FIFO. In per minute. A hard limit of the provider.

reportBatchItemFailures.title: Report batch item failures
reportBatchItemFailures.description: FunctionResponseTypes: ReportBatchItemFailures. A function that returns the records that failed has only those come back after the visibility timeout; the rest are deleted. Off, such a reply is ignored: the invocation succeeded, so the whole batch is deleted, the failed records with it. A FIFO batch keeps a failed record's later messages of the same group too, as a correct FIFO handler reports them.

throttleRetry.title: Throttle retry
throttleRetry.description: When the function is throttled, the mapping keeps the batch and tries again after this long, until the queue's visibility timeout runs out. AWS says Lambda backs off and retries but publishes no interval: this is an assumption. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

provisionedMinPollers.title: Provisioned mode: minimum pollers
provisionedMinPollers.description: 0 leaves provisioned mode off. Otherwise (AWS accepts 2 to 200) the mapping starts with this many dedicated pollers, each driving up to 10 concurrent invocations, and adds up to 1,000 invocations a minute. Overrides maximum concurrency, as in AWS. In pollers. A hard limit of the provider.

provisionedMaxPollers.title: Provisioned mode: maximum pollers
provisionedMaxPollers.description: Upper bound on pollers in provisioned mode: 100,000 concurrent invocations at 10,000. The AWS pages disagree on this maximum (2,000 on the parameters page, 10,000 on the newer scaling pages); the newer figure is used. In pollers. A hard limit of the provider.

originType.title: Origin type
originType.description: An S3 bucket does not offer the origin response timeout: it is not retried on a slow response. A custom origin is retried on a timeout for GET and HEAD. One of: custom (Custom HTTP origin (ALB, EC2, API Gateway...)), s3 (S3 bucket).

role.title: Role
role.description: Primary origins split the objects by this edge's weight, like cache behaviours by path. A secondary origin is only called when a primary fails the failover criteria, and only for reads. One of: primary (Primary (or an origin on its own)), secondary (Secondary (origin group failover)).

shield.title: Origin Shield
shield.description: Put Origin Shield in front of this origin: one more cache layer that collapses requests from every regional cache into one.

connectionAttempts.title: Connection attempts
connectionAttempts.description: How many times CloudFront tries a refused connection (and, for a custom origin, an origin that does not answer) before giving up or failing over. A hard limit of the provider.

responseTimeout.title: Response timeout
responseTimeout.description: How long CloudFront waits for the origin to answer before it drops the connection (a 504 once the attempts are used). Applies to custom origins. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes". The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

responseCompletionTimeout.title: Response completion timeout
responseCompletionTimeout.description: The longest CloudFront waits for the whole origin response across every attempt. 0 for no limit. When set it must be at least the response timeout. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

filterMatch.title: Filter policy match rate
filterMatch.description: The share of messages this subscription's filter policy lets through; the rest are filtered out and never delivered. 1 means no filter policy. Simulated messages carry no attributes or body to match, so this is a rate, not a rule. A fraction: 0.25 is 25%.

rawMessageDelivery.title: Raw message delivery
rawMessageDelivery.description: On: the subscriber gets exactly what was published. Off: SNS wraps it in a JSON envelope of about 1024 bytes (an assumption). AWS's own default is off; the simulator defaults to on so a design's message sizes are unchanged.

deadLetterQueue.title: Dead-letter queue
deadLetterQueue.description: When delivery finally fails (retries used up, or the endpoint refuses the message), send the message to the queue wired to this topic's dead-letter port instead of discarding it. The redrive policy of the subscription.

maxReceivesPerSecond.title: Delivery throttle
maxReceivesPerSecond.description: The throttle policy of an HTTP/S delivery policy (maxReceivesPerSecond): SNS holds deliveries back to this average rate per subscription, and held messages do not use up retries. 0 for no throttle. In msg/s.

parallelization.title: Concurrent batches per shard
parallelization.description: ParallelizationFactor: batches of one shard processed at the same time (records of one item stay in order). A hard limit of the provider.

maxRecordAge.title: Maximum record age
maxRecordAge.description: Records older than this are discarded instead of retried. -1 retries until the stream drops them (24 hours): a bad record blocks its shard that long. In s. A hard limit of the provider.

maxRetries.title: Maximum retries
maxRetries.description: Retries of a failing batch before its records are discarded. -1 retries until the record expires. A hard limit of the provider.

bisectOnError.title: Split failing batches
bisectOnError.description: A failing batch is split in two to isolate a bad record. Splitting doesn't use up retries.

retryBackoff.title: Retry backoff
retryBackoff.description: Wait before retrying a failed batch, doubling each time up to the cap below. AWS doesn't publish the schedule; an assumption. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

maxRetryBackoff.title: Retry backoff cap
maxRetryBackoff.description: An assumption: AWS doesn't publish it. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

eventTypes.title: Event types
eventTypes.description: Which changes this destination is subscribed to: s3:ObjectCreated:* (PUT, COPY, completed multipart upload), s3:ObjectRemoved:* (DELETE), or both. One of: all (Created and removed), created (Object created), removed (Object removed).

filter.title: Share matching the filter
filter.description: A notification can be filtered by key prefix and suffix. The simulator has no key names, so a filter is the fraction of matching events that it lets through: 1 is no filter, 0.1 is a filter that matches one object in ten. A fraction: 0.25 is 25%.

events.title: Event types
events.description: The matching event types of this event destination.

send.title: Send
send.description: SES accepted the message and will try to deliver it (also counted when delivery is then suppressed).

delivery.title: Delivery
delivery.description: The recipient's mail server accepted the message.

bounce.title: Bounce
bounce.description: A hard bounce, or a soft bounce SES has stopped retrying, or a send to a suppressed address.

complaint.title: Complaint
complaint.description: The recipient marked the message as spam.

reject.title: Reject
reject.description: SES accepted the message, found a virus in it and did not send it.

deliveryDelay.title: Delivery delay
deliveryDelay.description: A temporary problem delayed delivery; SES keeps retrying.

open.title: Open
open.description: The recipient opened the message (needs open tracking).

click.title: Click
click.description: The recipient clicked a link (needs click tracking).

latency.title: Network latency
latency.description: One-way; paid on the way there and back. Unless set, it is estimated from where the two nodes run.

mean.title: Average
mean.description: Typical time taken A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

cv.title: Variability
cv.description: Coefficient of variation: 0 is constant, 1 is heavily spread

origin.description: Where it came from when imported, so a re-import can find and merge it.

controller.description: A loop that watches a node and changes it while the design runs, such as an autoscaler.

target.description: The id of the node it changes.

scenario.description: What happens to this design: a timeline of faults and changes, and the checks that must hold.

description.description: What it shows. The first paragraph is its short blurb.

seed.description: Random seed for the run: the same design, scenario and seed always play out the same.

duration.description: How long to run. Required to run it.

warmup.description: Time to let the system settle before measuring: checks and summaries start after it.

scale.description: Multiply every client's request rate: 3 is three times the traffic.

overrides.description: Settings applied at the start, merged over the design's own.

timeline.description: What happens, and when. Each event does one thing; an event with only a note annotates the timeline.

at.description: When it happens, from the start of the run.

note.description: Says what this event is, in the timeline.

target.description: What breaks: node:<id>, edge:<id> or region:<placement> (region:aws:us-east-1).

fault.description: The fault: Outage (Rejects every call at once, like a connection refused or a stopped service. On a region, the whole region is down.) Errors (A fraction of calls fail with a server error after being processed.) Slow (Adds fixed latency to every call.) Blackhole (Calls vanish without a reply; callers wait out their full timeout.) Loss (A fraction of calls vanish without a reply.) Write it as Outage, Slow(250ms), Errors(20%), Loss(10%), or as an object { type: Slow, extra: 250ms }.

extra.description: A time: a number of seconds, or text such as 90s, 2m, 1h30m, 250ms or "2 minutes".

for.description: How long it lasts. Without it, the fault lasts until cleared.

id.description: A name to clear it by later.

clear.description: Lift a fault by the id it was injected with, or all of them (all).

set.description: Change a node's or an edge's settings while it runs.

settings.description: Settings, merged over what it already has.

account.description: Change the account quotas of a placement while it runs.

settings.description: Settings, merged over what it already has.

assert.description: What must hold. A run passes when every check does.

anyOf.description:
A check that must hold over the run (after the warm-up unless a window is given), in the check language:

<subject>.<metric>[:<aggregate>] <op> <value> [@ <from>..<to>]

subject   a node id; edge:<edge id>; or system (every client together)
metric    errorRatio | successRatio | throughput
          rate.<counter>          per-second rate of a counter: rate.ok, rate.fail, rate.fail.Throttled, rate.in, rate.sent
          total.<counter>         how many events in the window
          gauge.<name>            a gauge: gauge.depth, gauge.concurrent, gauge.inflight, gauge.cacheHitRate
          latency.<stat>          p50 | p95 | p99 | mean | max, of the 'latency' distribution (other distributions: dist.<name>.<stat>)
aggregate how to combine the window's frames: mean (default) | max | min | last | sum
op        < <= > >= == !=
value     a number, with optional unit: 500ms, 2s, 1.5%, 10/s
